prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
(empty)

New part:
S001: The Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies distribution circuits through transformer and feeder bays.
S002: The station automation boundary covers bay-level monitoring and control, station coordination, and the interfaces to external operating personnel and systems.
S003: Primary equipment, protection functions, and field wiring remain subject to their approved designs and operating limits.
S004: The Bay Automation Controller is assigned the project codename Juniper.
S005: The Bay Automation Controller performs bay-level sequencing, status evaluation, and control permissive checks.
S006: The Bay Automation Controller produces a Bay Status Digest for operational awareness.
S007: North Bay Controller and South Bay Controller provide bay-specific automation for their respective portions of the station.
S008: The Feeder Protection Relay detects feeder faults and initiates protection actions within its configured protection zone.
S009: The Feeder Protection Relay produces a Relay Diagnostic Note when its self-monitoring identifies a condition requiring engineering attention.
S010: Protection trips remain independent of routine bay-control commands so that a control-system failure does not inhibit fault clearing.
S011: The Breaker Control Unit executes authorized breaker operations and enforces its local electrical and mechanical interlocks.
S012: The Bay Automation Controller requests breaker operations only when the applicable operating mode and permissives allow them.
S013: Local control takes precedence when equipment is selected for local operation.
S014: Remote commands are subject to station authority, bay selection, interlocking, and equipment availability.
S015: The Station Supervisory Control System provides the station-level operating interface and supervisory coordination.
S016: The Station Gateway defines the communications boundary for authorized connections beyond the station automation network.
S017: The Satellite Time Receiver provides the station with a reference for time synchronization.
S018: The Sequence Event Archive retains operational event information for later review.
S019: The Engineering Workstation supports authorized configuration and maintenance activities under controlled access.
S020: The Maintenance Remote Terminal is limited to approved maintenance access and does not replace local operating authority.
S021: The Station DC System supplies control power to automation and protection equipment within its design capacity.
S022: The Control Room Operator directs routine station operation and verifies that commanded equipment states are appropriate.
S023: The Protection Relay Engineer maintains protection settings and evaluates relay performance within the approved change process.
S024: The Substation Field Crew performs field checks and equipment work under the applicable switching instructions and clearances.
S025: The supervisory architecture separates station-wide observation from local bay and protection functions.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
response:
{"summary":"The Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies distribution circuits through transformer and feeder bays. Its station automation boundary includes bay monitoring/control, station coordination, and interfaces to external operating personnel/systems; primary equipment, protection functions, and field wiring remain governed by approved designs and operating limits. Architecture separates station-wide observation from local bay/protection functions.
Bay Automation Controller (project codename Juniper) performs bay sequencing, status evaluation, and control permissive checks; produces Bay Status Digest for operational awareness; requests breaker operations only when applicable operating mode and permissives permit. North Bay Controller and South Bay Controller provide automation for their respective station portions.
Feeder Protection Relay detects feeder faults and initiates protection actions within its configured protection zone; produces Relay Diagnostic Note when self-monitoring identifies conditions requiring engineering attention. Protection trips must remain independent of routine bay-control commands so control-system failure cannot inhibit fault clearing.
Breaker Control Unit executes authorized breaker operations and enforces local electrical/mechanical interlocks. Local control takes precedence for equipment selected for local operation. Remote commands require station authority, bay selection, interlocking, and equipment availability.
Station Supervisory Control System provides station-level operating interface and supervisory coordination. Station Gateway defines the communications boundary for authorized connections beyond the station automation network. Satellite Time Receiver supplies the station time-synchronization reference. Sequence Event Archive retains operational event information for review. Engineering Workstation supports authorized configuration/maintenance under controlled access. Maintenance Remote Terminal permits only approved maintenance access and does not replace local operating authority. Station DC System supplies automation/protection control power within design capacity.
Control Room Operator directs routine operation and verifies commanded equipment states. Protection Relay Engineer maintains protection settings and evaluates relay performance under the approved change process. Substation Field Crew performs field checks/equipment work under applicable switching instructions and clearances."}
